defect: Two successful concurrent records could overwrite each other's snapshots; sync could publish an older derivative after another record.
behavior: Cooperating record/sync commands hold one persistent-file OS lock across state reads, validation and both publications. CLI record validation is also inside the lock. Contenders have a three-second acquisition budget and do not read or modify journal contents on timeout.
checks: Working tree clean before and after both committed-source executions
coverage: Real owned competing processes: record/record, record/sync, sync/record.
Bounded busy refusal with byte-identical journals, followed by successful retry.
Independent journals do not share a lock.
Canonical and coordination output destinations are refused, including normalized aliases.
Hard-linked coordination files refused on Windows and Linux; symlink counterpart passes on Linux.
Existing real os._exit73-after-canonical regression proves abandoned OS-lock recovery by a fresh CLI sync.

review.self_review: Read/validate/write exclusion, persistent inode identity, process exit/exception cleanup, fd validation, readonly-reader semantics and output guard reviewed.
review.independent: PENDING; this self-review is not independent approval.

limitations: MJ-REQ-008 stays PARTIAL; host/power-loss/container/browser restart breadth is not established by these tests.
Acquisition contention is bounded; arbitrary filesystem I/O or flush duration is not.
Only cooperating updated tools on the same local journal are coordinated; network filesystems, manual editors, older tools and separate Git worktrees are outside this proof.
The persistent coordination file requires planning-directory creation permission on first use and must not be removed/replaced while publishers may run.
Read-only validate/resume can observe an in-flight canonical/derived mismatch; repeat after the publisher finishes.
Already lost historical entries cannot be reconstructed automatically.
Local Ruff NOT_RUN because unavailable; required hosted policy/static checks remain mandatory.
acceptance: No result/criterion/denominator promotion. Canonical accounting requires a separately owned integration window.
